custom_logic_notes: This EA uses a state machine via MT5 GlobalVariables to track pending order placement across ticks. When a new VLT signal fires on a new bar, it sets GlobalVariable timestamps ('bs' and 'ss'). On subsequent ticks, if the GV timestamp matches the current bar, it attempts to place BuyStop/SellStop pending orders at High[1]+PendingLevel+Spread (buy) and Low[1]-PendingLevel (sell). If the GV timestamp is stale, it deletes the GV. Both BuyStop and SellStop are placed simultaneously (OCO-like behavior managed by code). When a position is open, opposing/opposite pending stop orders are deleted. The iVLT custom indicator (buffer index 2) determines signal existence — the indicator itself is not included in this source and must be obtained separately. The EA uses CSymbolInfo for price normalization and CTrade for order placement. Dead code exists: SignalOpenBuy(), SignalOpenSell(), SignalCloseBuy(), SignalCloseSell() all return false and are never called.
backtest_data_needs: Any symbol with 5-digit pricing, daily or intraday bars, 365 days minimum. Requires iVLT indicator source or pre-computed signal values.
python_conversion_notes: Major challenges: (1) The iVLT custom indicator must be reverse-engineered or sourced separately — buffer 2 at shift 1 produces non-EMPTY_VALUE on signal bars. (2) The pending order state machine using GlobalVariables must be reimplemented as a simple in-memory state dict keyed by bar timestamp. (3) Both BuyStop and SellStop are placed simultaneously per signal — this is OCO logic that must be handled when one fills (cancel the other). (4) Price normalization using Sym.NormalizePrice, Sym.Spread(), Sym.StopsLevel() must be replicated. (5) The SL/TP are calculated relative to the stop price, not current market price — important for backtest accuracy. (6) Pending order expiry is not set in the code — orders persist until filled or deleted by the CheckDelete logic. (7) The dead code functions (SignalOpenBuy etc.) can be ignored. Suggested approach: implement VLT indicator in Python first, then use vectorized signal detection with event-driven pending order simulation for accurate backtesting.
